answer: Payment sits in escrow until a jury grades the work, so nothing leaves the budget on an unverified claim. A replayed submission claws the escrow back to the payer, and no identity audits its own recruit, so a founder cannot route grading to a friend. A comet of a launch week buys no free pass either. Run the numbers: a farm needs one escrow per clone, a stranger jury per clone, and enough real work to pass grading, which is why the sparrow-sized operator outruns the hollow shell.
